problem: Loading a saved audio script replaced edited manual wording without confirmation. The same direct replacement existed in the saved-draft selector and bucket review; successful manual preparation also replaced pre-existing edits.

cases.expected: My unsaved local wording must remain available.
cases.actual: Researchers opened an ocean observatory. This saved story was prepared with partial source coverage.

change: One dirty-draft gate covers saved draft, saved take and bucket review. Preparing new text asks before dispatch only when it would replace edits. Failures keep the edit; existing asynchronous draft identity protection remains. No prompt for a clean or identical draft. Missing source record is treated as edited.

decision.pair: Steve and Elena, independent read-only proposals and one challenge/revision
decision.initial: Both recommended a shared conditional load guard; Steve initially preferred preserving edited text after generation, Elena initially preferred preflight confirmation.
decision.revised: Steve supported preflight confirmation to prevent dispatch on cancellation and avoid invisible results. Elena preferred preserving edited text after generation with a direct saved-result status/action.
decision.chosen: Preflight confirmation for dirty Prepare news text plus the shared explicit-load guard. It identifies the charge and replacement before dispatch and avoids a new persistent result-feedback state. Clean preparation stays direct.
decision.reservation: Elena preferred preserving edited text after generation to avoid another dialog. This preference is retained rather than reported as unanimous design agreement.
decision.artifactReview: Elena reviewed the actual implementation and returned no actionable findings.

scope.textProvider: substituted responses, including failure and success

limitations: This is controlled engineering evidence, not an observed listener session.
